$comment: Immutable prior-release lock artifacts. See README.md. Every field is checked by TestPriorReleaseFixturesAreImmutable; digests are SHA-256 of the file bytes.

fixtures.why: The oldest recoverable v1 shape: one extension pinned by a SINGLE scalar `integrity`, before per-platform `integrities` existed. It is the oldest lock a user can hold, so it proves the floor refusal reaches the earliest format.
The v1 shape at the release that introduced the CLI pin (LockFile.CLI). The extension entry carries BOTH the legacy scalar `integrity` and a one-platform `integrities` map.
The first lock this repository ever committed at v2 — the require-v3 cutover that made v2 the read floor. Its extension entry records NO taskContract.
A fully populated v2: `taskContract: 3` recorded plus two real per-platform archive digests.
The first v3 lock: it adds the `toolchains` dimension with six per-platform Go release digests. It is the newest recovered shape, so the ceiling test restamps it as a lock from the future.

gaps.reason: No v4 or v5 lock is recovered yet. v4 is covered by the in-package reader and writer tests and by the synthetic `v4Golden` in prior_release_test.go. v5 is covered as the OUTPUT of MigrateLockFileToCurrent for a lock that pins no toolchain, and by lockfile_v5_test.go: a lock that pins toolchains reaches v5 only through `putnami install`.

No lock committed to this repository has ever pinned the CLI (`putnami pin` writes one, but this workspace builds the CLI from source). The per-platform `cli.integrities` preservation is therefore proven against the in-package `v4Golden`, which is labelled synthetic where it is used.
